                "senderName": "NWS Kansas City/Pleasant Hill MO",
                "headline": "Flood Warning issued October 3 at 2:44PM CDT until October 7 at 11:09AM CDT by NWS Kansas City/Pleasant Hill MO",
                "description": "...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in\nMissouri...\n\nMissouri River at Glasgow affecting Saline, Chariton and Howard\nCounties.\n\n* WHAT...Moderate flooding is occurring and moderate flooding is\nforecast.\n\n* WHERE...Missouri River at Glasgow.\n\n* WHEN...Until Wednesday morning.\n\n* IMPACTS...At 25.0 feet, Farmland along the river floods. At 27.0\nfeet, Many agricultural levees are overtopped. Widespread flooding\nof rural areas occurs. Secondary roads and homes behind levees may\nbe inundated. The city park in Glasgow also begins to flood.\n\n* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...\n- At 2:30 PM CDT Saturday the stage was 27.0 feet.\n- Forecast...The river is expected to rise to a crest of 30.9 feet\nearly tomorrow afternoon.                 "description": "...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in\nMissouri...\n\nMissouri River at Boonville affecting Moniteau, Cooper, Howard and\nBoone Counties.\n\n* WHAT...Minor flooding is occurring and minor flooding is forecast.\n\n* WHERE...Missouri River at Boonville.\n\n* WHEN...Until Wednesday afternoon.\n\n* IMPACTS...At 21.0 feet, Low-lying rural areas along the river\nflood. At 23.8 feet, Easley River Road and Smith Hatchery Road\nbegin to flood. At 25.0 feet, Numerous farm levees are overtopped.\nFlooding of agricultural land and secondary roads occurs. Backwater\nflooding on Perche Creek causes flooding in McBaine.\n\n* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...\n- At 2:04 PM CDT Saturday the stage was 21.0 feet.\n- Forecast...The river is expected to rise to a crest of 27.0 feet\nearly Monday morning.                 "description": "...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in New\nMexico...\n\nRio Puerco Near Bernardo affecting Socorro County.\n\n* WHAT...Minor flooding is forecast.\n\n* WHERE...Rio Puerco near Bernardo.\n\n* WHEN...Until late tonight.\n\n* IMPACTS...At 19.5 feet, At the initial flood stage of 19.5 feet,\nthe water level in the Lower Rio Puerco will begin to threaten\nseveral homes and structures in the village of San Francisco\nbetween Interstate 25 and the Rio Grande.                 "description": "...The Flood Warning is extended for the following rivers in\nNebraska...\n\nTurkey Creek near De Witt affecting Saline and Gage Counties.\n\nTurkey Creek Near Wilber affecting Saline County.\n\n* WHAT...Minor flooding is occurring and minor flooding is forecast.\n\n* WHERE...Turkey Creek near Wilber.\n\n* WHEN...Until late Sunday night.\n\n* IMPACTS...At 15.0 feet, Portions of County Road O, located north of\nHighway 41, may begin to flood.\n\n* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...\n- At 7:45 AM CDT Saturday the stage was 14.5 feet.\n- Bankfull stage is 11.0 feet.\n- Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours ending\nat 7:45 AM CDT Saturday was 15.1 feet.\n- Forecast...The river is expected to fall below flood stage late\ntomorrow evening and continue falling to 3.1 feet Thursday\nmorning.\n- Flood stage is 12.5 feet.\n- Flood History...This crest compares to a previous crest of 14.5\nfeet on 06/18/1990.\n- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood",

                "headline": "Flood Warning issued October 3 at 8:42AM CDT until October 6 at 1:18AM CDT by NWS Omaha/Valley NE",
                "description": "...The Flood Warning is extended for the following rivers in\nNebraska...\n\nBig Blue River Near Crete affecting Saline County.\n\nBig Blue River At Beatrice affecting Gage County.\n\n* WHAT...Minor flooding is occurring and minor flooding is forecast.\n\n* WHERE...Big Blue River at Beatrice.\n\n* WHEN...Until late Monday night.\n\n* IMPACTS...At 21.0 feet, At this level the West Scott baseball\nfields begin to flood.\n\n* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...\n- At 7:45 AM CDT Saturday the stage was 19.4 feet.\n- Bankfull stage is 16.0 feet.\n- Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours ending\nat 7:45 AM CDT Saturday was 19.4 feet.\n- Forecast...The river is expected to rise to a crest of 21.5 feet\ntomorrow morning. It will then fall below flood stage Monday\nmorning.\n- Flood stage is 18.0 feet.\n- Flood History...This crest compares to a previous crest of 21.3\nfeet on 09/30/1923.\n- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood",
                "instruction": "Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood\ndeaths occur in vehicles.\n\nMotorists should not attempt to drive around barricades or drive cars\nthrough flooded areas.\n\nBe especially cautious at night when it is harder to recognize the\ndangers of flooding.\n\nPlease report observed flooding to local emergency services or law\nenforcement and request they pass this information to the National\nWeather Service when you can do so safely.\n\nAdditional information is available at water.noaa.gov.\n\nThe next statement will be issued this evening at 845 PM CDT.",

                "description": "* WHAT...Flooding caused by recent excessive rainfall continues.\n\n* WHERE...Along the West Fork Big Blue River in Southeastern York\nCounty in east central Nebraska and Northwestern Fillmore County in\nsouth central Nebraska...\n\n* WHEN...Until 100 PM CDT Sunday.\n\n* IMPACTS...Flooding of rivers, creeks, streams, and other low-lying\nand flood-prone locations is imminent or occurring.\n\n* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...\n- At 824 AM CDT, the gauge along the West Fork Big Blue River north\nof Grafton was at 12.7 feet, which was above minor flood stage of\n11.0 feet. As a result, fairly widespread flooding of pastures\nand fields immediately adjacent to the river continues, including\ndownstream through the McCool Junction area.                 "headline": "Flood Warning issued October 3 at 9:14AM EDT by NWS Melbourne FL",
                "description": "...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in Florida...\n\nSt Johns River Near Astor affecting Lake and Volusia Counties.\n\n.The St Johns River at Astor is forecast to dip from Minor Flood\nStage to Action Stage this weekend. Towards the middle of next week,\nanother rise into Minor Flood Stage is forecast due to increasing\nrain chances and a return of northerly winds.\n\nFor the St. Johns River...including Astor...Minor flooding is\nforecast.\n\n* WHAT...Minor flooding is forecast.\n\n* WHERE...St Johns River near Astor.\n\n* WHEN...Until further notice.\n\n* IMPACTS...At 2.3 feet, Many docks become submerged along the river\nand in canals in the Astor community. Water enters yards of\nproperties on Bartram Road, Holiday Circle and along Wild Hog Road\non the Lake County side. In Volusia County, water encroaches yards\nof homes on the river side of Alice Drive. No wake zones are in\neffect from near the South Moon Canal to approximately 800 feet\nsouth of the Riverview lodge.\n\n* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...\n- At 8:30 AM EDT Saturday the stage was 2.3 feet.\n- Bankfull stage is 2.0 feet.\n- Forecast...The river is expected to remain right around flood\nstage at 2.3 feet through today. It will then fall into Action\nStage for a couple of days before rising back into flood stage\ntowards the middle of next week. Additional rises through Minor\nFlood Stage are forecast thereafter.\n- Flood stage is 2.3 feet.\n- Flood History...This crest compares to a previous crest of 2.5\nfeet on 05/28/2023.\n- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood",
                "instruction": "Motorists should not attempt to drive around barricades or drive cars\nthrough flooded areas.\n\nCaution is urged when walking near riverbanks.\n\nAdditional information is available at www.weather.gov.\n\nThe next statement will be issued this evening at 1100 PM EDT.",

                "description": "...The Flood Warning is extended for the following rivers in\nNebraska...\n\nWest Fork Big Blue River Near Dorchester affecting Saline and\nSeward Counties.\n\n.This gauge has already crested and river levels will continue to\nfall.\n\n* WHAT...Minor flooding is occurring and minor flooding is forecast.\n\n* WHERE...West Fork Big Blue River near Dorchester.\n\n* WHEN...Until Sunday afternoon.\n\n* IMPACTS...At 18.0 feet, Though only minor flooding is occurring at\nthe gage, upstream near Beaver Crossing more severe flooding is\nlikely ongoing.\n\n* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...\n- At 4:00 AM CDT Saturday the stage was 16.5 feet.\n- Bankfull stage is 15.0 feet.\n- Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours ending\nat 4:00 AM CDT Saturday was 17.6 feet.\n- Forecast...The river is expected to fall below flood stage late\nthis evening and continue falling to 8.8 feet early Thursday\nmorning.\n- Flood stage is 15.0 feet.\n- Flood History...This crest compares to a previous crest of 16.5\nfeet on 06/25/2010.\n- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood",
                "instruction": "Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads.
